# `AppParCurves` Rust API contract (generated by `tools/judgegen.py`, module `appparcurves`)

This is the API the generated judge `tests/appparcurves.rs` replays; the translator must provide exactly these items in `occt_port::appparcurves` (C++ names mapped by the rule below; `docs/api-appparcurves.names.tsv` lists every Rust name used). Everything is derived mechanically from the OCCT 8.0.1 headers of the package.

## Conventions

* Scalars are `f64`, `i32`, `bool`; a C++ enum is a fieldless Rust enum in declaration order (`*self as i32` is the C++ ordinal; variant = constant without the package prefix, CamelCase); gp value types are `occt_port::gp` types (`gp::Vec` is `gp_Vec`); a `TColgp_Array1OfPnt` / `TColStd_Array1OfReal` ... input is `&[T]` and an output is `Vec<T>` (lower bound 1); a two-dimensional array is `plib::Array2<T>`.
* A C++ `const T&` parameter is `&T`, a by-value parameter is `T`. Non-const reference parameters are out-parameters: they are not parameters in Rust, the function returns them after the return value, in order (`(ret, out1, out2)`; a single value is returned bare, none is `()`). A non-const method takes `&mut self` and the harness prints the object again after the call; a const method takes `&self`.
* Methods that can raise `Standard_Failure` return `Result<_, Error>`; this list shows `Result` where the oracle saw a `throws` line or the header documents a raise. The harness accepts a plain value or a `Result` from every call; a `throws` line requires an `Err`, so a method that can raise must return `Result`. Constructors of classes of the package are associated functions (`new`, overloads `new_<suffix>`). Static methods of the class `AppParCurves` and free functions are functions of the module.
* Rust has no overloading. The name of an overload is `snake_case(C++ name)` plus: `_<count>` when the overloads differ in parameter count, then `_<types>` of the parameters whose type differs among overloads with the same count (`lin`, `circ2d`, `real`, `int`, `arr_pnt`...), `_mut` for the non-const twin of a const method with the same parameters, `_b`, `_c` for a remaining clash. `names.tsv` overrides: `Class::Method(sig)<TAB>name` or `Class::Method/N<TAB>name`.
* The oracle links the sources of the package compiled **with the checks enabled** (the shipped OCCT libraries are built with `-DNo_Exception`, which compiles every `Raise_if` out: a call that the documentation says raises would read garbage there). A `throws` line therefore means "the documented check fires"; the Rust API must return `Err`.
* Objects of the package's classes are checked by their *snapshot*: after the call the harness reads every zero-argument const getter of the class (listed per class below) and compares the values; a getter that raises must return `Err` (printed `x`).
* The harness builds gp inputs with these `occt_port::gp` calls (all part of the already translated gp API): `Pnt::new`, `Dir::new(x,y,z)` (normalizes, fails on zero), `Ax1::new(Pnt, Dir)`, `Ax2::new(Pnt, Dir, &Dir)`, `Ax3::from_ax2(&Ax2)` + `x_reverse/y_reverse`, `Lin::from_axis`, `Circ/Elips/Hypr/Parab::new(Ax2, ..)`, `Pln::new(Ax3)`, `Cylinder/Cone/Sphere/Torus::new(Ax3, ..)`, `Mat::from_values`, `Quaternion::from_components`, `Trsf::new` + `set_rotation/set_scale/set_translation/set_mirror`, and the 2D forms (`Ax22d::from_dirs`, `Circ2d::from_ax22d` ..., `Lin2d::from_ax2d`, `Mat2d::from_columns`, `Trsf2d::new` + setters). Outputs are read through `x()/y()/z()`, `location()/direction()/x_direction()/y_direction()`, `position()/axis()`, `radius()` ..., `value(r, c)` (see the `Emit` impls in the test).
